title: Deduplication preserves evaluation of non-tautological clauses
statement: Let $c$ be a clause over the variables $x_0,\dots,x_{n-1}$ — a list of literals read as their disjunction, where a literal evaluates to $x_i$ if positive and $\lnot x_i$ if negated. Suppose $c$ is not tautological, meaning it contains no two literals on the same variable with opposite signs. Then for every Boolean assignment $x \colon \{0,\dots,n-1\} \to \{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, the clause obtained from $c$ by keeping only the first literal on each variable evaluates to the same truth value as $c$ itself.
hypotheses_covered: c is a list of literals (a clause) over n variables
c is not tautological (no two literals share a variable with opposite signs)
x is a Boolean assignment on the n variables
replaced:
If a clause $c$ is not tautological, then for every assignment $x$ the disjunction of
the literals of $\mathrm{dedupClauseVars}\,c$ has the same value as the disjunction of
the literals of $c$.
